title_yt: A Stranger Offers You a Coin Flip. Would You? #Shorts
title_fb: A stranger offers you a coin flip. Would you take it?
hook: What if a stranger offers you a coin flip?
open_loop: Line 6 asks outright: 'Why does the stranger want you to quit?' (right after the tails bonk, about 60% in). It is paid off only in line 7 and the line 8 payoff, the last ~9 s: over time each flip pays you twenty five dollars, so the stranger loses. The $25 is not said or shown before line 7.
payoff: Your brain makes a one hundred dollar loss feel like nearly two hundred, so you say no. But over many flips each flip pays you twenty five dollars, which is why the stranger wants you to quit. 'Your brain says no. The math says flip.'

disclaimer_on_screen: 'Not financial advice' badge from scene 7 to the end. Framed as a brain/decision thought experiment, not advice to gamble.

facts_used.claim: In the coin toss (win $150 / lose $100), most people decline.
Most people reject the 50/50 win $150 / lose $100 flip even though it pays on average (corroborating).
Meta-analysis mean loss-aversion coefficient 1.955, so a $100 loss feels like about $195 ('nearly two hundred').
Losses are treated as about twice as large as an equivalent gain; the ratio varies by context, hence 'nearly'.
Over many flips, +$25 per flip on average for you and -$25 for the stranger (zero-sum). A single flip is still a 50/50.

math_check: Per flip: 0.5*150 - 0.5*100 = 75 - 50 = +$25 on average (stranger -$25, zero-sum). Felt loss = 1.955*100 = $195.50 -> 'nearly two hundred' (95% range $182.00-$210.20, all above the $150 win, so the brain says no). 'Over time' is the hedge: one flip is still a true 50/50.
changes_from_previous: Note 1 (you/your): line 2 'Heads, you win one hundred fifty dollars.', line 3 'Tails, you lose one hundred.', line 4 'Your brain makes losing one hundred feel like nearly two hundred.', lines 5-7 use 'you'. Benny stays on screen as the viewer's avatar; no more 'Benny says / his brain'.

Note 2 (explicit open loop): new line 6 'Why does the stranger want you to quit?' is planted right after the tails bonk and the 'Quit!' bubble, and only answered in line 7 ('Because each flip pays you twenty five dollars, over time.') with the '-$25 HIM' GULP gag.
Note 3 (turn-back beat): line 4 ends with Benny running away, then new line 5 'You turn back and flip.' shows him stopping and turning before the first flip.

Note 4 (concrete, not abstract): removed 'on average'. Now 'each flip pays you twenty five dollars, over time' with coin rain showing many flips; the new one-line payoff 'Your brain says no. The math says flip.' (line 8) sits before the A/B ending.

Note 5 (length): 70 spoken words = 30.4 s at 2.3 w/s, 9 lines, 9 scenes. Trimmed by dropping the separate 'Benny keeps flipping' and 'It costs the stranger' lines (the stranger loss is now shown on screen in scene 7) and 'dollars' on the tails line.
